Featured case studies

Problems I’ve solved in research operations.

Each one follows the same structure: the challenge, my role, the actions I took, the results, and the skills that carry over to clinical research.

Case 1

Research operations · Voxelmaps

Participant qualification and screening

01Challenge

Participants were being booked into studies without meeting the required qualifications. Each one had to be turned away, which wasted session time and slowed projects down.

02My role

As UX Operations Manager, I oversaw participant scheduling, onboarding, and progress tracking, so making sure booked participants met each study’s requirements was part of my job.

03Actions taken

I reviewed the booking process and screening documents and traced the problem to communication and documentation gaps between recruiters and the research team. I updated the screening documents with the correct eligibility requirements and trained recruiters on what to check and who to contact with questions.

04Results

Participant rejection rates went down, recruiters and the research team worked from the same accurate information, and more sessions ran with qualified participants.

Transferable research skills

Participant recruitmentParticipant screeningEligibility verificationResearch documentationRecruiter and team communicationData quality

Why it matters in clinical research: clinical studies depend on the same discipline, with clear eligibility criteria, accurate documentation, and well-trained staff.

Case 2

Research operations · Tata Elxsi

Venue recruitment and coordination

01Challenge

Recruiting venues for research sessions was slow. Each venue's status, qualification details, and next steps weren't kept in one place, so venues were rejected late and work stalled between vendors, venue owners, and our team.

02My role

As Project Manager, UX Operations, I worked with multiple venue recruitment vendors and venue owners and was responsible for getting qualified venues ready on schedule.

03Actions taken

I built a shared tracker showing each venue's status, qualifications, and next steps. I used it to give vendors clear requirements so venues met compliance standards before they were submitted, and to keep schedules and stakeholders aligned.

04Results

Venue recruitment delays dropped, fewer venues were rejected, and everyone worked from the same accurate data, which closed communication gaps and kept projects moving.

Transferable research skills

Research logisticsScheduling and coordinationStakeholder communicationTracking systemsDocumentationProcess improvement

Why it matters in clinical research: selecting and qualifying research sites works the same way, with clear standards, shared tracking, and steady communication with outside partners.

Digital health & accessibility

Projects that make health technology easier to use.

Tracing CarePatient Portal & EHR Practice Platform
In progressVisit the site

A safe place to practice using a patient portal and basic EHR tasks, filled with realistic but made-up patients and records. I’m designing and building it on my own.

Problem

Many healthcare jobs expect EHR familiarity, but most EHR training environments are limited to employees, so students and career changers have nowhere to practice. Older adults learning patient portals face a similar gap: practicing on a real account means real health information, and with scams on the rise, people and organizations are rightly careful about who sees it.

Approach

Use fictitious but realistic data so anyone can practice without risk. Model the lessons on the flow of most real patient portals, so learners can repeat the same steps on their own accounts. Design for accessibility from the start, with bigger text and hints for when someone gets stuck.

Solution

  • Guided practice Available now
    Six everyday portal tasks for patients and families, step by step.
  • Explore freely Available now
    Move around the portal as Robin Merriweather, a made-up patient. No login required.
  • Staff training Planned
    Guided screens for clinical, billing, and admin learners.

Progress and next steps

The site is live at tracing-care.com, with a learning page that leads into the practice portal. Next, I plan to make the portal an installable web app, add at-home learning features, and then release iOS and Android apps.

Patient PortalsEHR TrainingDigital Health LiteracyAccessibility

About

Research operations professional, moving into clinical research.

I’m a research operations professional with more than five years of experience coordinating participant-based studies, from moderating research sessions to managing participant scheduling, screening, and onboarding across multiple sites.

I’m now transitioning into clinical research, drawn to patient-centered research and to the operational work that keeps studies organized and on track. In every role, I care about efficient processes and healthcare that is accessible to everyone.

My story

The Journey Behind My Work.

  1. 🇧🇷

    The beginning

    Born in Brazil, wired for curiosity

    Before I ever thought about workflows or efficiency, I was a kid obsessed with how things fit together. Legos were basically my first job: structure, logic, and the satisfaction of making pieces click into place. That instinct has followed me everywhere.

  2. 🗽

    Age 14: New York

    Everything changed overnight

    At 14, my family moved to New York. New language, new culture, new everything. It was humbling, and looking back, one of the best things that ever happened to me. You learn real adaptability when you have no choice but to figure it out.

  3. 🎸

    2012: Tennessee

    Memphis, logistics, and thinking at scale

    I got married and settled in Tennessee, in the middle of one of the world's great logistics hubs. Watching complex operations run (or fail to run) at that scale sparked a lasting interest in coordination, efficiency, and making systems actually work.

  4. 🌉

    2016: California

    Operations, evolved

    On the West Coast, the work got sharper: less about moving boxes, more about how people and systems interact. I moved into research operations, where I learned to coordinate participants, sites, and teams, and to find and fix the friction that slows work down.

  5. 🌴

    2026: Florida

    Closer to family, clear on the mission

    Moved to Florida to be closer to family. Showing up for the people who shaped me also clarified my direction: bringing my operations experience to healthcare and clinical research.

  6. Today

    Where it's all coming together

    Today I'm transitioning into clinical research, building on my research operations background and recent GCP training. Through Solara Vita and Tracing Care, I also help older adults and learners feel confident with health technology. The kid who loved Legos is still in there, just building bigger, more inclusive systems now.
